catalogue_requests.summary: Send one MoveRobot velocity and duration goal to the ROS 2 /move_robot action server.
catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogue class carries the pinned MoveRobot wire. cap.motion.mobile_base.v1 takes linear_velocity, angular_velocity and duration_s and requires distance_m and heading_rad outputs that the native action does not report; cap.motion.joint_position.v1 is a joint-position array with reached and tolerance_rad outputs and has no velocity/duration goal. Using either class would change the native request or invent an output. The extension preserves the three flat float64 goal fields and the bool success/string message result.

WHAT WAS AUTHORED: a configuration-only RosDriver over the pinned ROS 2 native action /move_robot with type my_robot_interfaces/action/MoveRobot (src/my_cpp_pkg/src/move_robot.cpp:27-32; the fully qualified type is at src/my_cpp_pkg/src/move_robot.cpp:8; the fields are in src/my_robot_interfaces/action/MoveRobot.action:1-11). The endpoint is the upstream relative token move_robot configured at the root with source_name, and every binding has source_ref/type_ref. The goal fields linear_vel_x (m/s), angular_vel_z (rad/s) and duration (s) are mapped unchanged; the result mapping exposes the native bool success and string message; the success predicate is success == true. The device is mode simulated, risk R2 (mobile base), kind robot.mobile_base. The package uses the x-cap id x-cap.will0103.move-robot.v1 because no catalogue class preserves the native request and result; the inline schema and catalogue request record that gap. The fake is a ROS-free RecordingRosTransport at F0: it answers send_action_goal and cancel_action_goal for /move_robot, records one serial goal queue, publishes one terminal action_result, and can hold goals or inject a protocol error, an application failure or malformed terminal values. It runs no Gazebo Harmonic world, physics, sensors, ros_gz_bridge, controller, action-server timing loop or ROS graph. Its state values and negative-path strings are test data, marked # placeholder; the upstream success and cancel strings are quoted from move_robot.cpp:136 and :146.
